court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A restrictive covenant on a residential subdivision limiting buildings to use "as a private dwelling house or habitation" bars operation of a hotel on the land, since "private dwelling" excludes an inn or hotel and the covenant restricts use, not merely exterior form. The court found the defendant had structurally enlarged his building and was operating it as a hotel furnishing board and lodging for pay, and enjoined that use as a violation of the covenant.

notes: Enforcement is via private restrictive covenant rather than a municipal police-power ordinance, but the doctrinal posture (hotel/lodging use treated as an impermissible commercial intrusion into a residential-only tract) matches the adverse file.
